Weighted least-squares update of the cellGLoc mean structure

Source: R/cellgloc_utils.R
dot-gloc_update_B.Rd

Column j of B is fitted on the design using that column's cell weights as observation weights. Cross-response dependence is handled by the scatter step, not here.

.gloc_update_B(X, U, W, U_main = U, patterns = NULL, warn = TRUE)

Arguments

X

\(n x p\) numeric matrix of continuous variables, may contain NA.

U

\(n x q\) design matrix from .gloc_design.

W

\(n x p\) matrix of cell weights in [0, 1].

U_main

the main-effects version of U, from .gloc_design_aux; the default, U itself, stands for a design without interaction terms.

patterns

the level combinations, from .gloc_design_aux: each row's combination (id, NA where a row's categories are unknown), the pure design row of each combination (P, and P_main for U_main) and its labels. NULL takes every distinct row of U as a combination (.gloc_row_patterns).

warn

TRUE raises the design warnings here; FALSE attaches them to the result as the attribute "gloc_design", when there is anything to report, for .gloc_warn_design.

Value

a \(q x p\) matrix of coefficients.

Details

A column left with no cell of positive weight (e.g. every weight is zero) cannot be fit at all; rather than silently returning NA into downstream matrices, this case warns (naming the offending column) and falls back to the unweighted median of that column's finite values, or to 0 if none exists. A column with fewer usable cells than design columns warns too and uses the median of those cells. Either constant is put through the design (.gloc_const_coef), so every row gets it whether or not the design has an intercept column.

A design that is rank deficient on the rows a column is fitted from is fitted on a maximal set of linearly independent design columns, chosen by the same pivoted QR decomposition qr.solve() uses; a full-rank design takes exactly the arithmetic of qr.solve(), so its result is unchanged bit for bit. Identification is decided on the cells whose weight exceeds .gloc_w_floor times the column's largest: a fit that is full rank on them keeps that full-rank result, tiny cells included, and a fit that is rank deficient on them takes the path below on them alone. The data then determine the fitted mean only of the level combinations that a fitted row has or whose pure design row lies in the row space of the fitted rows, and those keep it exactly. Every other combination – a level for which the variable has no cell with positive weight, under any coding of the factors, an unseen combination of partly aliased factors, or a combination absent from the data – is filled in the null space of the fitted rows' design (.gloc_estimable, .gloc_fill_null): first the combinations that occur in the data, by one least-squares step, then the absent ones, only in the null-space directions that step leaves free, so an absent combination never moves a row that exists. Identification and targets are decided on level combinations (patterns), not on rows: a probability-weighted row whose combination is unknown (an NA id) is never a combination itself, and its fitted mean follows from the filled coefficients. The target is the variable's weighted mean over the fitted rows, except that under a design with interaction terms a combination that the main-effects design U_main identifies on the same rows takes that design's fitted mean. Where several combinations share one unidentified direction, it is their average over the combinations that meets the target: under ~ g1 + g2 with a level of g1 never observed, that level's combinations keep the g2 effects between them. The fitted means this gives do not depend on how the factors are coded or ordered, nor on whether combinations absent from the data are enumerated. Aliased columns that change no fitted mean (two identical factors) warn as duplicates, naming neither a column that is zero on every fitted row nor one of an unidentified combination. Unidentified combinations that occur in the data (all of them, when some row's combination is unknown) warn once per reason, naming the variables, the combinations and what the fit does with them. With warn = FALSE the diagnostics are returned instead, and imputeCellGLoc raises them once, from its final iterate.

Correction, recorded rather than deleted: until 7.4.1 a rank-deficient design silently kept only a weighted mean in B[1, j], assuming column 1 is the intercept. With a factor duplicated, the x1 group means came back flat at 0.39 against 0.17, 3.92 and -3.15, and diag(Sigma) was 8.5 against 0.87; with a level that never records x1 they came back flat at 15.44 under ~ f, and 14.97, 0 and 0 under ~ f - 1. The first 7.4.1 fix filled design columns one at a time and recognised an unobserved level only as an all-zero column. It missed a never-observed reference level under treatment coding (level a came back 30.72 against a truth of 10), divided by zero under sum contrasts, and sent a combination missing only from an interaction to the grand mean (14.03 against 30).
